draft.title: International treaties and Australia
card: A treaty is a formal agreement between countries. A human rights treaty sets out rights that the countries agree to respect.
Australia signs a treaty and then ratifies it. This binds Australia as a nation under international law, and it is made by the executive government.
A treaty does not automatically become part of Australian law. It binds people and courts here only when parliament passes a statute that includes it.

Example: Australia is a party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. Its rights can be enforced in Australian courts only to the extent that parliament has put them into Australian law.
draft.remember: A signed treaty binds Australia internationally. It binds locally only once parliament legislates.

a.q: Australia ratifies a human rights treaty, but parliament has passed no law about it. What is the effect in Australian courts?
opts: The treaty does not bind people or courts here
The treaty binds courts here as soon as it is ratified
The treaty binds only the High Court, not other courts
The treaty binds only public servants, not other people
a.why: A treaty becomes enforceable in Australian courts only when parliament makes it part of Australian law. Ratifying it binds Australia internationally, but ratification alone does not create rights that a court here can enforce.
a.clue: Which body has to act before a treaty becomes local law?

b.q: Priya says a treaty Australia ratified last year lets her sue a business in a Victorian court. Parliament has not passed any law about it. Why is she likely to fail?
opts: Parliament has not made the treaty part of Australian law
Treaties apply only to governments, never to businesses
Only the High Court can hear cases about treaties
Australia has not agreed to be bound by the treaty
b.why: Priya is likely to fail because the treaty has not been made part of Australian law by a statute, so a court here cannot enforce it. The last option is tempting, but ratifying does bind Australia under international law. That is a different thing from binding people locally.
b.clue: Ratifying binds Australia as a nation. What else is needed for local courts?

a.best: The treaty does not bind people or courts here

b.best: Parliament has not made the treaty part of Australian law
